title: |x| = 2x − 3 has one solution
caption: y = |x| and y = 2x − 3 meet only at (3, 3). The other case, x = 1, would need −x = 2x − 3 with x < 0, and the lines do not meet there.
alt: The V-shaped graph y = |x| and the line y = 2x − 3 crossing once at (3, 3).
description: Draw y = |x|, a V with its point at the origin.
Draw y = 2x − 3, a line with gradient 2 crossing the y-axis at −3.
They meet once, at (3, 3); x = 1 is not a solution because |1| = 1 but 2(1) − 3 = −1.
